text:
sanjay: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of odd SSO events over the last 12m. Several internal high-priv accounts got MFA pushes from geographically disparate IPs within a ~2m window. Auth logs show the same `device_header_hash` reused across sessions but paired with different IPs. Suspect header-reuse or proxy replay. I'm starting containment now (revoking sessions for affected users). Any immediate red flags?

maria: Who are the affected accounts? can we avoid a broad user comms blast until we confirm? :thinking_face:

sanjay: Affected (internal aliases): infra_build, plateng_admin, onboarding_test, db_migration. Query snippet: ```select user, device_header_hash, ip, ts from auth.sso.events where ts > now()-interval '15 minutes' and device_header_hash in ('hsh-9f3e','hsh-9f3e') order by ts;``` shows same hash with IPs in CA, NL, and APAC.

emily: On it. Running session revokes for those four users now: `./infractl sessions revoke --user infra_build,plateng_admin,onboarding_test,db_migration --force` — kicking off, ETA ~30s. Posting logs.

ir-bot: session-revoke: infra_build (ok), plateng_admin (ok), onboarding_test (ok), db_migration (ok) — initiated by emily at 2734567918.

leo: Good containment. Quick checks: 1) did we just rotate any KMS keys or SSO connector certs in the last 24h? 2) check our SSO proxy headers implementation — header normalization bug could cause hash collision. Also consider temporary RBAC tighten: deny console_write for members of `sso-internal-admins` until we confirm.

cori: Enabling full audit logging (auth+token events) for the next 7 days and shipping to longterm audit bucket. Will also add an immediate alert for `device_header_hash` reused across >3 geos within 10m.

sanjay: Confirming no KMS rotations in last 72h (checked key rotation log). We did push a small proxy config change 3h ago on staging only, but not prod. No recent deploys to the SSO connector service in prod.

emily: ops note: we saw a CI job that reuses a headless browser image in the last 30m; it intentionally reuses a custom UA and header shim. Investigating if that explains the duplicate header for some infra accounts.

leo: If CI is reusing the header shim, it could explain the reuse but not the geo variance unless CI runners are distributed. Still, treat as potential token-replay attempt until proven otherwise. I'll add a WAF rule to block requests with `device_header_hash: hsh-9f3e` to the SSO endpoint for 1h as a precaution. Anyone object?

maria: No objections. Please include an exception path for the CI runners if we confirm. Also let's avoid blocking traffic to customer-facing endpoints.

ops-oncall: Confirming no customer-facing outages or auth errors reported. This looks internal-first.

sanjay: Rotated the SSO connector service principal secret (new secret pushed to vault) and forced re-auth for connector sessions. Also triggered a rekey for the ephemeral signing key used in header generation (not master KMS key).

cori: Audit logs now include raw header values (obfuscated) and correlate device_header_hash -> session_id -> ip. Exported a CSV and shared to #eng-sec-private.

leo: Post-containment plan: 1) keep WAF block for 1h, 2) short-term RBAC: revoke console write for `sso-internal-admins` until tomorrow morning, 3) full investigation into CI runner header shim and distributed runners, 4) rotate any linked OAuth client secrets that saw anomalous auth events.

sanjay: I'll draft the internal comms for impacted employees and a short incident note. Also opening an IR ticket with severity P2.

emily: Follow-up: if CI explains this, we still need to harden header generation (add per-run nonce) and update docs.

maria: Assigning follow-ups: leo (WAF + RBAC change), cori (audit retention + alert tuning), emily (CI investigation + mitigation), sanjay (IR ticket + internal comms). I'll own the post-incident write-up.

sanjay: Thanks all. No customer impact found. Will update IR ticket with timeline and next steps. :white_check_mark:
